questions.q_txt: Which of the following vehicles is it prohibited to use on a public road?

options.txt: A vehicle with a horn louder than 70-decibels.
A vehicle without a front windshield.
A tank used in warfare.
A vehicle displaying dealer's plates.

questions.explanation: Under Thai motor vehicle law, a registered vehicle must not be altered in its body or any part to differ from its registered particulars before being used on public roads (rule_id=135, section 1.8). A vehicle without a front windshield is structurally incomplete and deviates from its registered specifications, making it prohibited for road use. The other options—horn volume, warfare tanks, and dealer red plates—are either not prohibited outright or are specifically permitted under defined conditions.

questions.q_txt: When the green car wants to turn, what should be done?

options.txt: Slowly turn right, carefully minding other cars.
Stop and wait for the yellow car to pass then turn after.
Wait for both the blue and yellow cars before turning.
Turn right immediately.

questions.explanation: At this T-intersection, the green car wants to turn right from a minor road onto the main road where the yellow car is traveling straight (southbound). According to rule_id=215, when turning right into a minor road (or from one), the rider/driver must yield to traffic on the main road and wait until there is a sufficient gap in traffic before turning — meaning the green car must stop and let the yellow car pass first. The blue car is already stopped/parked and not actively moving through the intersection, so it does not need to be waited for separately.

questions.q_txt: Which of the following statements is true?

options.txt: You may allow unlicensed drivers to user your vehicle.
It is prohibited to drive a vehicle for which the annual tax has not been paid.
You may allow someone else to use your driver license.
You may display license plates that you have had made yourself.

questions.explanation: Under the Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522, vehicles must be properly registered and have annual taxes paid before they can legally be used on public roads; driving a vehicle with unpaid annual tax is therefore prohibited (rule_id=134). The other options are all illegal: allowing an unlicensed person to drive your vehicle, lending your driver's licence to another person, and displaying self-made licence plates are all violations of Thai traffic law. Only option 2 correctly states a true legal requirement.

questions.q_txt: You are required to turn on your headlights:

options.txt: To request right of way in an emergency.
To request right of way in an emergency.
When heavy fog restricts visibility to less than 150 meters.
When it is raining.

questions.explanation: Thai traffic law requires drivers to turn on their headlights when heavy fog reduces visibility to less than 150 meters, ensuring other road users can see your vehicle and helping prevent collisions in low-visibility conditions. While the provided rule chunks do not explicitly state this fog-visibility threshold, this is a standard provision in the Road Traffic Act covered in the Thai driving manual. Options 1 and 2 (requesting right of way in an emergency) relate to emergency vehicle signals, not headlight requirements, and option 4 (rain alone) does not automatically trigger a headlight requirement under the law.

questions.q_txt: When you see this sign, you should:

options.txt: Stop and allow oncoming traffic to pass before proceeding.
Reduce your speed and watch for oncoming traffic.
Proceed with caution
Not enter the road ahead

questions.explanation: The sign shown is the 'Give Way to Oncoming Traffic' regulatory sign — a red circle with a red upward arrow and a black downward arrow — meaning drivers facing it must yield absolute priority to vehicles coming from the opposite direction. As a regulatory sign under Thai traffic law (rule_id=164), it imposes a mandatory obligation: you must stop and allow all oncoming traffic to pass before you proceed, not merely slow down or proceed with caution. This aligns with the principle in rule_id=179 regarding yield/stop signs, where drivers are required to fully stop and wait until it is safe.

questions.q_txt: When descending a steep grade or hill, you should:

options.txt: Turn off your engine
Shift to neutral
Keep your foot on the brake
Use a low gear

questions.explanation: When descending a steep grade, you should use a low gear to take advantage of engine braking, which helps slow the motorcycle and reduces reliance on the brakes. As stated in rule_id=213, riding downhill in a low gear utilizes engine braking to share the workload of the braking system, because continuous braking on a long downhill slope can cause the braking system to overheat and malfunction, potentially leading to accidents. Turning off the engine, shifting to neutral, or keeping your foot on the brake alone are all unsafe practices on steep descents.

questions.q_txt: The dividing lines in the middle of the road pictured indicate:

options.txt: Move the yellow car off the road and turn on emergency flashes.
The driver of the yellow car in the picture may make a U-turn.
The driver of the yellow car in the picture may not pull into the right lane to overtake another vehicle.
The driver of the yellow car in the picture may turn into the right lane.

questions.explanation: The dashed yellow centre line shown in the image is a 'Normal Traffic Direction Dividing Line' (rule_id=186), which separates traffic travelling in opposite directions. Drivers must stay on the left side of this line and may only cross it to make a right turn or overtake — but crucially, overtaking is only permitted when it is safe and legal to do so. Because the image shows oncoming traffic (the pink car) in the right lane, the yellow car's driver may not pull into the right lane to overtake, making option 3 correct.

questions.q_txt: Where is it not permitted to make a U-turn?

options.txt: Within 150 meters of a bridge.
In the spaces between traffic islands.
Where another vehicle is following at a distance of less than 150 meters.
On a bridge

questions.explanation: Under Section 55 of the Road Traffic Act, drivers are prohibited from stopping a vehicle on a bridge or in a tunnel (rule_id=151). Since making a U-turn requires the vehicle to maneuver and momentarily occupy the roadway in ways that would constitute stopping or obstructing traffic on a bridge, U-turns on bridges are not permitted. The other options (150 meters from a bridge, between traffic islands, or when a vehicle is following within 150 meters) are not the correct prohibited location specified by the law.

questions.q_txt: Where is it prohibited to make a U-turn?

options.txt: In the spaces between traffic islands.
In an intersection.
Where another vehicle is following at a distance of less than 150 meters.
Within 150 meters of the base of a bridge.

questions.explanation: Under Section 55 of the Road Traffic Act, drivers are prohibited from stopping a vehicle at an intersection (rule_id=151); by the same principle, making a U-turn at an intersection is also prohibited, as it creates dangerous conflict points with crossing and oncoming traffic. The other options—spaces between traffic islands, a following vehicle within 150 meters, or within 150 meters of a bridge—are not listed as prohibited U-turn locations under Thai traffic law.

questions.q_txt: In addition to his/her driving license, a driver must have at hand which document while driving.

options.txt: National ID card
Social security card
Copy of the car's registration
Copy of the house registration

questions.explanation: Under the Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522 (covered in Chapter 1, rule_id=134), a driver must carry the vehicle's registration document (the 'car registration book' or a copy of it) along with their driving licence whenever operating a vehicle on public roads. This requirement ensures that inspectors can verify the vehicle is properly registered and legally permitted for use, as outlined in the registration and use-of-vehicles provisions. The other options—national ID, social security card, or house registration—are not required documents for driving.

questions.q_txt: A driver violates the road traffic law and receives a ticket, within how many days must he pay the fine?

options.txt: 7 days
10 days
15 days
30 days

questions.explanation: Under the Road Traffic Act B.E. 2522, when a driver is issued a ticket for a traffic violation, they must pay the prescribed fine within 7 days of receiving the ticket. Failure to pay within this period can result in further legal proceedings. While the provided rule chunks cover various traffic penalties (such as fines for violating traffic signals per rule_id=192), the specific 7-day payment deadline is a core provision of the Road Traffic Act that drivers must remember.

questions.q_txt: A temporary driving license is valid for how many years?

options.txt: 1 year
2 years
3 years
5 years

questions.explanation: Under Thai motor vehicle law, a temporary driving license is issued to first-time applicants and is valid for 2 years. During this period, the holder must comply with all traffic regulations; after the 2-year period, they may convert it to a standard driving license valid for 5 years. None of the provided rule excerpts explicitly state this duration, but option 2 (2 years) is the correct answer per Thai licensing regulations.

questions.q_txt: How much additional money will be charged to a vehicle that does not pay annual tax within the stipulated time limit?

options.txt: 1% per month
5% per month
1% per year
5% per year

questions.explanation: Under Thai vehicle registration regulations, owners who fail to pay their annual vehicle tax by the deadline are subject to an additional surcharge of 1% per month on the unpaid tax amount. This penalty accumulates monthly until the tax is paid, incentivizing timely compliance. None of the provided rule chunks directly address this provision, but it is a well-established rule under the Thai Motor Vehicle Act.

questions.q_txt: How many years old must the car be before inspection is required when making the annual tax payment?

options.txt: 3 years
5 years
7 years
10 years

questions.explanation: Under the Thai Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522, when paying the annual road tax, vehicles that are 7 years old or older are required to undergo a vehicle inspection first. This rule ensures that older vehicles remain in a safe and roadworthy condition before being permitted to continue operating. The annual tax payment provisions are covered under the Motor Vehicle Act referenced in the manual's Chapter 1.

questions.q_txt: What is the speed limit within municipal limits, Bangkok, and Pattaya?

options.txt: 70 Km/H
80 Km/H
90 Km/H
100 Km/H

questions.explanation: Under the Highway Act (rule_id=138), motorcycles and other standard motor vehicles must not exceed 80 km/h when driven within the Bangkok Metropolitan Area, Pattaya City Area, or any municipal area. Outside those areas the limit drops to 70 km/h, which is why option 2 (80 km/h) is correct for the in-city scenario asked about here.

questions.q_txt: What is the speed limit outside municipal limits, Bangkok and Pattaya?

options.txt: 70 Km/H
80 Km/H
90 Km/H
100 Km/H

questions.explanation: According to the Land Traffic Act provisions cited in the manual (rule_id=138), motorcycles may travel at up to 80 km/h within the Bangkok Metropolitan Area, Pattaya City, or municipal areas, but outside those areas the limit rises to 90 km/h. However, the question asks specifically about outside municipal limits, Bangkok and Pattaya, where the prescribed maximum speed for motorcycles is 90 km/h, making option 3 correct. Always observe any posted signs that may set a lower limit for specific zones.

questions.q_txt: To park on the left driving lane, what is the maximum distance from the pavement to park or stop the vehicle?

options.txt: Not exceeding 20 centimeters
Not exceeding 25 centimeters
Not exceeding 30 centimeters
Not exceeding 35 centimeters

questions.explanation: According to the Road Traffic Act, when parking on the left side of the roadway, the driver must position the left side of the vehicle parallel to and no more than 25 centimeters from the road edge or shoulder (rule_id=151, rule_id=216). This rule prevents motorcycles from squeezing into the gap between the parked vehicle and the road edge, as also noted in safe parking guidelines (rule_id=217).

questions.q_txt: Who is the person exempted from wearing motorcycle helmet when driving?

options.txt: Seniors over 65
Traffic officers
Motorcycle passengers
Novice, monk

questions.explanation: Under Section 122 of the Road Traffic Act, the general rule requires all motorcycle riders and passengers to wear a safety helmet, but the law explicitly exempts monks, novices, ascetics, and clergy (or followers of other religions) who wear cloth or other head coverings according to their customary traditions (rule_id=159). Traffic officers, seniors, and passengers are not granted this exemption — in fact, the rider is legally responsible for ensuring passengers wear helmets (rule_id=214). Therefore, the correct answer is novices and monks.

questions.q_txt: What is the maximum passenger for motorcycle?

options.txt: 1 passenger
2 passengers
3 passengers
4 passengers

questions.explanation: Thai law explicitly states that a motorcycle rider may carry only one passenger (rule_id=214, Section 12.2: 'the law stipulates that a motorcycle rider may carry only one passenger'). This is reinforced by Section 122 of the Road Traffic Act, which requires both the rider and that single passenger to wear a safety helmet (rule_id=159). Carrying more than one pillion rider is therefore prohibited.

questions.q_txt: How many years old must the motorcycle be before inspection is required when making the annual tax payment?

options.txt: 1 year
3 years
5 years
7 years

questions.explanation: Under the Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522, motorcycles that are 5 years old or older are required to pass a vehicle inspection before the annual road tax payment can be made. This ensures that older vehicles remain roadworthy and meet safety standards. The table of contents (rule_id=129) references the 'Annual Tax Payment' section of the Motor Vehicle Act, where this requirement is established.

questions.q_txt: Vehicles which can be registered must have the following characteristics:

options.txt: The car must have the correct fittings and passed a vehicle inspection.
The car must have the correct fittings.
Vehicles which have passed a private vehicle inspection.
Cars purchased from general car dealers.

questions.explanation: According to the Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522 (rule_id=134), vehicles brought into use must be registered, and registration requires that the vehicle has the correct fittings and has passed a vehicle inspection. Simply having correct fittings alone, passing a private inspection only, or being purchased from a dealer is not sufficient — both conditions (correct fittings and passing an official vehicle inspection) must be met for a vehicle to be eligible for registration.

questions.q_txt: Which item is correct?

options.txt: Motorcycle that has reached 5 years of life, wishing to renew annual taxes must bring the car to a private condition examination center.
The car has 5 years of service life. Those wishing to renew their annual taxes must have the car inspected at a private inspection facility.
Motorcycle that has reached 7 years of life, wishing to renew annual tax must bring the car to be inspected at a private condition.
Car with a lifetime of 10 years, wishing to renew the annual tax must have the car to be checked at a private condition.

questions.explanation: Under Thai motor vehicle regulations, a motorcycle that has reached 5 years of age must be brought to a private vehicle inspection center (สถานตรวจสภาพรถเอกชน) before its annual road tax can be renewed. Option 1 correctly identifies both the vehicle type (motorcycle) and the age threshold (5 years). Options 3 and 4 state incorrect age thresholds (7 and 10 years respectively), while option 2 refers generically to 'car' rather than specifically to motorcycles.

questions.q_txt: How many years old does the applicant need to be to hold a temporary car driving license?

options.txt: 15 years old (completely)
18 years old (completely)
20 years old (completely)
22 years old (completely)

questions.explanation: Under Thai driving licence regulations, an applicant must be at least 18 years old (completely) to qualify for a temporary car driving licence. This minimum age requirement is established by the Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522 and related land transport regulations, which set 18 as the threshold for adult driving eligibility for private passenger vehicles. None of the provided rule chunks directly state this age requirement, but it is a foundational rule in Thai traffic law.

questions.q_txt: What is the penalty for anyone who drives a car without a driver’s license?

options.txt: Fine no more than 1,000 baht.
Imprisonment of not more than 1 month or fine of not more than 1,000 baht or both.
Fine no more than 2,000 baht.
Imprisonment of not more than 3 months or fine of not more than 2,000 baht or both.

questions.explanation: Under the Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522, driving a vehicle without a driver's license carries a penalty of a fine not exceeding 2,000 baht. This fine-only structure (with no imprisonment option) is consistent with the penalty levels established throughout the Motor Vehicle Act for similar administrative violations, as seen in provisions covering vehicle transfer, relocation, and modification notifications. Options involving imprisonment or higher fines apply to different offences under other acts such as the Road Traffic Act or Highway Act.

questions.q_txt: What is the safety zone mean?

options.txt: The area that the driver can take the car through.
Districts where pedestrians can cross paths without stopping to wait.
The area has a mark indicating that the driver is safe to continue driving.

The area in the car park marked with a clearly visible sign at all times for for pedestrians crossing the path to stop waiting or allowing people to get in or out of the car to stop and wait before crossing over.

questions.explanation: According to the official definition in the Thai Road Traffic Act (rule_id=140), a 'safety zone' is an area within the roadway that is clearly marked and visible at all times, designated for pedestrians crossing the road to stop and wait, or for persons boarding or alighting from vehicles to stop and wait before continuing to cross. This matches option 4 exactly, distinguishing it from a general crossing area or a zone where drivers are permitted to proceed.

questions.q_txt: When the officer extending any of his arm to the same level as shoulder and pose his hand perpendicular to the ground, what does this mean?

options.txt: The driver approaching from the direction of the arm must stop the vehicle.
The driver who approaches from the behind direction of the officer must stop the vehicle.
The driver approaching from the direction of the arm must continue forward.
The driver who approaches from the behind direction of the officer must continue forward.

questions.explanation: According to rule_id=162 (Manual p.35, Hand Signals, item 2), when a traffic officer stands and extends either arm out at shoulder level with the palm raised upright (perpendicular to the ground), drivers approaching from the side of that extended arm must stop their vehicles. The image shows exactly this gesture — one arm extended horizontally at shoulder height with the palm upright — meaning vehicles coming from the direction the arm points toward are required to stop.

questions.q_txt: How far must the driver drive from the car in front?

options.txt: Enough to be able to stop the car safely if necessary
No less than 5 meters
No less than 10 meters
No less than 20 meters

questions.explanation: The correct answer is that a driver must maintain enough distance from the vehicle ahead to be able to stop safely if necessary. This principle is reflected in the manual's guidance on following distance, which emphasizes the 3-second interval rule and maintaining adequate space to react and brake safely (rule_id=204). A fixed minimum distance like 5, 10, or 20 meters would not account for varying speeds and road conditions, so the law requires a distance sufficient for a safe stop in any situation.

questions.q_txt: In which areas is a driver permitted to make a U-turn?

options.txt: Roadway marked with a no U-turn sign
On a bridge
150 meters distance from the foot of a bridge
A safety zone

questions.explanation: Thai traffic law prohibits U-turns in several locations, including on a bridge, at a safety zone, and anywhere a no-U-turn sign is posted (rule_id=166). However, a driver is permitted to make a U-turn at a point that is at least 150 meters away from the foot of a bridge, since that distance places the vehicle safely clear of the bridge restriction zone. Rule_id=210 also notes that U-turn points are high-risk areas, reinforcing that only lawful, designated locations should be used.

questions.q_txt: When arriving at the railroad and there is a passing train, what should the driver do?

options.txt: Stop waiting for the signal light and turn on the emergency light.
Give a warning signal and drive through.
Drive through quickly.
Stop the car at least 5 meters from the railroad.

questions.explanation: Thai traffic law requires drivers to stop at least 5 meters away from a railroad crossing when a train is passing, ensuring a safe distance from the moving train. Driving through quickly or giving a warning signal and proceeding would be dangerous, and simply turning on emergency lights without maintaining the required distance does not satisfy the legal safety requirement. None of the provided rule chunks directly cite the railroad crossing rule, but the correct answer aligns with standard Thai Road Traffic Act provisions on railroad crossings (stopping at least 5 meters from the track).

questions.q_txt: What is the maximum blood alcohol level for driving?

options.txt: Not exceeding 50 mg percent
Not exceeding 60 mg percent
Not exceeding 70 mg percent
Not exceeding 80 mg percent

questions.explanation: Under Thailand's Road Traffic Act B.E. 2522, drivers are prohibited from operating a vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration exceeding 50 mg percent (50 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood). None of the provided rule chunks directly state this limit, but it is a core provision of Thai traffic law covered in Chapter 1 on laws related to driving. Exceeding this limit constitutes drunk driving and is subject to legal penalties.

questions.q_txt: What is the penalty for driving while detecting alcohol in the body more than the legal limit?

options.txt: Imprisonment of not more than 3 months or a fine of 1,000 to. 50,000 baht.
Imprisonment of not more than 1 year or a fine of 5,000 to. 20,000 baht or both.
Fine not more than 5,000 baht.
Fine not exceeding 10,000 baht.

questions.explanation: Under the Road Traffic Act B.E. 2522 (Section 43 bis), driving while blood alcohol concentration exceeds the legal limit carries a penalty of imprisonment of not more than 1 year, or a fine of 5,000 to 20,000 baht, or both. This is stricter than ordinary traffic violations (which typically carry fines up to 1,000 baht) because impaired driving poses a severe risk to public safety. None of the provided rule chunks explicitly cover this penalty, but it is a core provision of Thai traffic law that drivers must know.

questions.q_txt: Which is correct?

options.txt: The truck must drive in the rightmost lane.
The passenger truck must drive in the rightmost lane.
Changing the lane to the right or left. Do not look at the left or right mirror.
Motorcycles must drive in the left lane of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Under Section 35 of the Traffic Act and the motorcycle handbook, motorcycles must drive in the leftmost lane (or the lane nearest to the bus lane) on roads divided into two or more lanes in the same direction (rule_id=144, rule_id=210). Rule_id=210 further specifies that motorcycles must use the left lane and may only move right temporarily to overtake, returning to the left lane afterward. The other options are incorrect: trucks and passenger vehicles also use the leftmost lane (not the rightmost), and changing lanes requires checking mirrors (not skipping them).

questions.q_txt: Cars with slow speeds, what should the driver do?

options.txt: Drive on the shoulder
Drive on the right edge
Drive close to the left edge
Can drive on both the left and right

questions.explanation: Under Section 35 of the traffic law (rule_id=144), a vehicle traveling slowly or at a speed lower than other vehicles in the same direction must drive as close to the left edge of the roadway as practicable. This is reinforced by the general lane-use rule (rule_id=209), which states that all drivers must use the left lane, and by safe driving guidance (rule_id=240) that instructs drivers to keep as far left as possible. Therefore, a slow-moving vehicle should drive close to the left edge of the road.

questions.q_txt: What should the driver do when seeing this mark?

options.txt: Be extra careful. Then stop the car.
Be extra careful
Drive slowly if you see that it is unsafe for other cars or pedestrians in the way ahead. Have to stop the car before reaching the line, make way.
Increase caution and park the car

questions.explanation: The inverted white triangle is Thailand's 'Give Way' (Yield) sign, which requires drivers to slow down and assess the situation ahead. According to the road-surface yield marking rules (rule_id=189) and the yield line rules (rule_id=188), if proceeding would be unsafe for other vehicles or pedestrians on the cross road, the driver must stop before the yield line and give way — exactly matching option 3. Simply being 'extra careful' or stopping unconditionally are both incorrect; the obligation to stop is conditional on whether it is unsafe to proceed.

questions.q_txt: When this road marking is found what should the driver do?

options.txt: Do not turn left or turn right.
Do not drive straight or turn right.
Drive in one direction on the left.
Car on the solid line must not pass or straddle the solid line But the car on the side of the dotted line may overtake when it is considered safe.

questions.explanation: The marking shown is a combination line: one side has a solid yellow line and the other has a dashed yellow line. According to the Thai manual (rule_id=186), a 'No-Overtaking Traffic Direction Dividing Line' with this mixed solid/dashed appearance means that the driver on the side of the solid line must not cross or straddle it to overtake, while the driver on the side of the dashed line may overtake when it is safe to do so. This is exactly what option 4 describes.

questions.q_txt: When this sign is found what should the driver do?

options.txt: Let the driver drive fast Lines allow to go immediately.
The driver to drive slowly. Then overtake.
Always stop before reaching the transverse line.
Let the driver slow down and speed up first.

questions.explanation: The road marking shown is a Stop Line — a wide solid white line drawn across the roadway at a T-intersection or junction. According to the traffic markings rules (rule_id=188), when a stop sign is present or a traffic signal commands a stop, the driver must stop the vehicle before reaching the stop line. Therefore, the correct action is to always stop before reaching the transverse (stop) line.

questions.q_txt: What does this sign mean?

options.txt: No trucks of all kinds.
Motorcycles are prohibited.
All cars are prohibited.
All vehicles are allowed to pass.

questions.explanation: The sign shown is a circular prohibition sign with a red border and a red diagonal slash over a black motorcycle silhouette — this is the standard 'No Motorcycles' sign. According to rule_id=166 (item 16), the 'No Motorcycles' sign means all types of motorcycles are prohibited from passing in or out of the road zone where the sign is installed. Therefore, option 2 is correct.

questions.q_txt: When seeing this sign what should the driver do?

options.txt: A car with at least 3 people can use this lane.
A car with 1 person can enter this channel.
No more than 3 people enter this lane.
There are 2 people sitting in. Can enter this lane.

questions.explanation: The sign described is a white diamond shape painted on the road surface with the numeral '3' inside, which is the High-Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane marking. According to rule_id=190, a white diamond on the road with a number inside indicates a High-Occupancy Vehicle lane, meaning only vehicles carrying no fewer than the specified number of occupants (in this case, 3) may use that lane. Therefore, a car with at least 3 people is permitted to use this lane.

questions.q_txt: When seeing this sign what should the driver do?

options.txt: Drive fast Increase caution The road ahead has a narrow bridge.
Drive slowly. Increase caution The way ahead is a steep downhill.
Drive quickly. Increase caution The road ahead is a steep hill way.
Drive slowly. And be extra careful The way ahead must use the left bypass.

questions.explanation: The orange diamond sign shows a road curving left with wavy lines (water) on the right, indicating the right side of the road ahead is flooded/submerged. Because the right lane is inundated, drivers must slow down, exercise extra caution, and use the left bypass to avoid the flooded section — consistent with the general warning sign principle of slowing down and following the indicated detour direction (as seen with 'Left Detour' signs in construction zones). This matches option 4: drive slowly, be extra careful, and take the left bypass.

questions.q_txt: Driving through a community, school, or crowded place what should be done?

options.txt: Honk the horn and accelerate to get away fast.
Slow down honk and use caution.
Honk the horn and slow down the speed.
Slow down and use caution when driving.

questions.explanation: When driving through a community area, school zone, or crowded place, the correct approach is to slow down and use caution — without necessarily honking the horn. Rule 238 explicitly states 'Reduce speed and exercise more caution than usual' for community areas and school zones, and Rule 180 reinforces that near schools drivers should slow down, watch for children, and actually refrain from using horns during school hours. Honking is not required and may even be prohibited near schools, making option 4 the most accurate and complete answer.

questions.q_txt: Driving during heavy rain, how should you drive?

options.txt: Reduce the speed carefully. Turn on the headlight and wiper.
Drive carefully and turn on the car headlights and fog lights.
Gradually drive and turn on the high beam..
Stop the car on the road. And wait until the rain stops and then continue driving.

questions.explanation: During heavy rain, drivers must reduce speed carefully and turn on headlights and wipers to maintain visibility and control — this aligns with rule_id=237, which instructs using low speed in rain, and rule_id=223, which emphasizes that speed control is critical on wet roads to prevent skidding. Rule_id=224 further confirms that drivers should slow down when visibility is poor, such as during rain. Stopping on the road (option 4) is dangerous and unnecessary, fog lights or high beams (options 2 and 3) are not the correct response for rain.

questions.q_txt: Which is NOT a way to show appreciation to other drivers?

options.txt: Bend the head to show gratitude.
Smile to show appreciation.
Turn on the high beam to show gratitude.
Raise your right hand to raise your eyebrows to show gratitude.

questions.explanation: According to the manual's section on Expressing Gratitude (referenced in rule_id=244 and the table of contents in rule_id=132), appropriate ways to show appreciation to other drivers include nodding your head, smiling, or raising your right hand. Turning on the high beam is not a gesture of gratitude—it is a headlight control function used for visibility or signaling purposes (rule_id=200), and using it to 'thank' another driver could actually blind or confuse them, making it an inappropriate and potentially dangerous action.

questions.q_txt: When should the driver use the horn?

options.txt: Say hello to other known drivers.
Prevent danger or accident that may occur from the car.
Speeding the front car to drive faster.
Chase pedestrians crossing the crosswalk.

questions.explanation: The horn is a safety warning device that should only be used to prevent danger or potential accidents, not for social greetings, pressuring other drivers, or chasing pedestrians. As confirmed in rule_id=233, drivers should 'use the horn as a warning if suspicious or unsure' when hazards such as parked car doors or vehicles pulling out pose a risk. Similarly, rule_id=229 notes that when encountering cyclists, a driver 'should maintain a sufficient distance, use the horn, and make eye contact to ensure that the cyclist has noticed your vehicle' — always in the context of safety, not convenience or aggression.

questions.q_txt: While driving If the car bonnet is open what should the driver do?

options.txt: Reduce speed and park on the side of the road To close the bonnet neatly.
Swerve the car to the side immediately To close the bonnet neatly.
Sudden braking.
Step on the accelerator so the bonnet is bumped off.

questions.explanation: When the car bonnet unexpectedly opens while driving, the driver must reduce speed gradually and safely pull over to the side of the road before closing it. Swerving suddenly, braking abruptly, or accelerating would all create serious hazards for the driver and other road users. This aligns with the manual's guidance on safe parking procedures (rule 217) and the principle of decelerating safely without sudden actions (rule 203), ensuring the vehicle is moved off the traffic surface before addressing the problem.

questions.q_txt: If heavy rains occur so that the path cannot be clearly seen what should the driver do?

options.txt: Speed up and get through the rainy areas quickly.
Park the car immediately.
Turn on the headlights, accelerate through the heavy rain.
Park the car in a safe area. Turn on the car headlights and turn on the emergency lights.

questions.explanation: When heavy rain makes the road impossible to see clearly, the safest action is to pull over in a safe area, turn on the headlights so your vehicle is visible to others, and activate the emergency flashers to warn other road users — this aligns with the emergency parking guidance in rule 217, which instructs drivers to turn on emergency flashers and move off the traffic surface to avoid obstructing or endangering others. Rule 237 also notes that in poor visibility conditions like rain, drivers should manage speed and stopping carefully, and rule 223 reinforces that in poor visibility (rain, fog) extra caution is required. Speeding up or continuing to drive when you cannot see the road is dangerous and not recommended under any of these guidelines.

questions.q_txt: When driving up or down a steep slope which gear should be used?

options.txt: Low gear
High gear
Neutral gear
Any gear

questions.explanation: When driving up or down a steep slope, you should use a low gear. As rule_id=201 explains, riders should select a gear appropriate to the engine power required, such as when riding uphill on a steep road. Rule_id=213 further specifies that when riding downhill or on a slope, a low gear should be used to apply engine braking, which reduces speed and shares the workload of the braking system — preventing brake overheating and potential malfunction that could lead to accidents.

questions.q_txt: When driving at night what should the driver do?

options.txt: Leave more distance between cars than usual.
Try to drive close to the front car so that the front car can clearly see our car.
Turn on the emergency light while overtaking the front car.
Use high lights all the way of driving.

questions.explanation: At night, visibility is reduced, so drivers must increase their following distance to allow more time and space to react to hazards. Rule 223 explains that in conditions of poor visibility (such as rain, fog, or darkness), the safe following distance should be extended beyond the normal 3-second rule — counting 4 seconds or more. Rule 234 further reinforces this by advising that at night you should drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights, meaning a greater gap from the vehicle ahead is essential for safety.

questions.q_txt: Which situation uses emergency lighting appropriately?

options.txt: Turn on emergency lights while fog is down.
Turn on emergency lights when going to turn left at an intersection without traffic lights.
Turn on emergency lights to let other drivers know that they will run straight to.
Turn on Emergency lights when the car is parked on the shoulder.

questions.explanation: According to rule_id=217, when a driver must park in an emergency, the very first step is to turn on the emergency flashers to alert other road users so they can take evasive action, and the vehicle should be moved off the traffic surface. Rule_id=237 further clarifies that emergency flashers should NOT be used while driving in rain, and rule_id=215 confirms that normal turn signals (not emergency lights) are used when turning at intersections. Therefore, the correct and appropriate use of emergency lighting is when the vehicle is parked on the shoulder in an emergency situation.

questions.q_txt: Which statement is correct?

options.txt: Lubricating oil should not be added to petrol.
Oil filling should be added during the day.
We cannot mix 95 octane together with 91 octane.
The best oil is the most expensive oil.

questions.explanation: According to the motorcycle handbook's guidance on inspecting motorcycle readiness (rule 196), engine oil and fuel are treated as completely separate systems — engine oil is checked independently and must never be mixed into the petrol tank. Adding lubricating oil to petrol would contaminate the fuel system and damage the engine, making option 1 the correct statement. The other options are incorrect: mixing 95 and 91 octane petrol is generally acceptable, oil can be filled at any time of day, and the best oil is not necessarily the most expensive.

questions.q_txt: Which tire inspection is correct?

options.txt: 1 month
2 month
3 months
At least once a week

questions.explanation: According to the motorcycle handbook (rule_id=196), a good rider must regularly inspect the motorcycle's readiness before every ride, including checking tire pressure, tread depth, lights, horn, engine oil, and chain. Tires specifically must be checked to ensure they are not flat or leaking and that tread depth exceeds 1.6 mm. This pre-ride inspection routine implies tires should be checked at least once a week (or before each ride), making option 4 the correct answer.

questions.q_txt: If a battery terminal has stains. Which method below is the best solution?

options.txt: Use warm water to wash and apply grease
Use vinegar to wash
Use lemon juice to wash
Use distilled water to wash

questions.explanation: Battery terminals develop corrosion or sulfate stains over time, which can impede electrical contact. The correct approach is to clean the terminals with warm water to dissolve and remove the deposits, then apply grease (such as petroleum jelly) to coat the terminals and prevent future corrosion. The other options (vinegar, lemon juice, distilled water) are either too acidic or insufficient to properly clean and protect the terminals.

questions.q_txt: Who has to wear seat belts while traveling in a car for life safety?

options.txt: Drivers and passengers aged over 12 years old because they can wear seat belts.
The driver and passenger of the front seat only.
All drivers and passengers, both adults and children, front and back seats.
Drivers and passengers Except for the elderly and children younger than 12 years old.

questions.explanation: Under Thai traffic law, all drivers and passengers in every seat — front and back, adults and children — must wear seat belts. Section 123 of the Road Traffic Act requires the driver to fasten their own seat belt and ensure front-row passengers do the same, while rule_id=247 further specifies that passengers of any height (including those under 135 cm) must be secured with a seat belt or equivalent restraint regardless of which row they occupy. There are no blanket exemptions based on age or seating position, making option 3 correct.

questions.q_txt: Which aspect to pay special attention to do while driving through water?

options.txt: To heat the engine
Keep the car at a constant speed
To increase the speed of the car
To prevent the engine from shutting down

questions.explanation: When driving through water, the primary concern is keeping the engine running, as water can cause the engine to stall or shut down. According to rule_id=237, drivers should use low speed when driving through rain or water, which helps maintain engine operation and prevents water from being forced into the engine intake. Maintaining a steady, controlled low speed is the key technique to prevent the engine from shutting down in these conditions.

questions.q_txt: Which of the following is correct for nighttime driving?

options.txt: Turn on the high beam all the time while driving.
Turn on the emergency light at all times while driving.
Drive as fast as usual.
Drive slower than normal or not faster than the sight.

questions.explanation: At night, visibility is significantly reduced, so drivers must slow down to a speed at which they can stop safely within the distance they can actually see ahead — this is the principle of 'not driving faster than your sight line.' Keeping high beams on at all times (option 1) is incorrect because it blinds oncoming drivers, using emergency flashers while driving (option 2) is a traffic violation as noted in rule 237, and maintaining normal daytime speed (option 3) is dangerous when visibility is limited. Rule 222 reinforces that poor visibility conditions demand extra caution and reduced speed, especially for less experienced drivers.

questions.q_txt: Which is correct about driving fuel efficiency?

options.txt: The car will save more fuel if it runs at higher speeds.
The car will save fuel if driving at a constant speed.
The car will save more fuel if accelerating the engine frequently.
The car will save more fuel if it runs. With unstable speeds.

questions.explanation: Driving at a constant speed is the most fuel-efficient approach because it avoids the extra energy wasted during repeated acceleration and deceleration cycles. High speeds increase aerodynamic drag and engine load, while frequent acceleration or unstable speeds cause the engine to consume more fuel than necessary. Maintaining a steady, moderate speed keeps the engine in its most efficient operating range.

questions.q_txt: If you want to drive straight past you should be careful and how to act?

options.txt: Slow down the car and let the car on the right hand to pass first.
Speed up the engine to pass first.
Drive at the same speed.
Continue driving as we have right of way.

questions.explanation: The image shows a driver approaching an intersection intending to go straight, with a red car visible on the right side. Under Thai traffic law (rule_id=161, Section 22(4)) and the right-of-way rule (rule_id=239), when proceeding through an intersection—especially with a green arrow or when going straight—you must drive with caution and yield to vehicles coming from the right, as they are considered to have arrived first. Therefore, you must slow down and let the car on the right pass first before proceeding straight.

questions.q_txt: Which is the correct meaning of the blind spot?

options.txt: The front area of the car that the driver can’t see.
The back area of the car that the rear view mirror cannot capture.
The area that the driver can’t see clearly while driving.
The left area. Of the car that the driver can not see.

questions.explanation: A blind spot is defined as any area around the vehicle that the driver cannot see clearly while driving — it is not limited to just the front, rear, or one side. As noted in rule 214, motorcycle riders must periodically check blind spots by looking over their shoulder before pulling out, turning, or changing lanes, and should avoid riding in positions that fall within a car's blind spots. Rule 228 further reinforces this by describing techniques to reduce blind spots in all directions around the vehicle, confirming that blind spots can exist in multiple zones, not just one specific area.

questions.q_txt: When driving down a steep slope The driver should use low gear because of what reason?

options.txt: To increase the power of the car
To slow the speed of the car
To reduce the heat of the engine
To increase the speed of the car

questions.explanation: When driving down a steep slope, using a low gear engages engine braking, which helps slow the vehicle without relying solely on the brakes. As stated in rule 213, riding downhill in a low gear utilizes engine braking to reduce speed and share the workload of the braking system. This is critical because continuous brake use on a long downhill slope can cause the braking system to overheat and malfunction, potentially leading to accidents.

questions.q_txt: When seeing this sign what should the driver do?

options.txt: Should drive slowly and be careful The road ahead is currently being explored on the road surface or in the bus lane.
Drive quickly. Be extra careful when people are working.
Drive fast. Increase caution. The machine is working.
Drive slowly. Increase caution explore buildings.

questions.explanation: The yellow diamond sign showing a person operating a surveying instrument (theodolite) on a tripod is the official 'Road Survey' (สำรวจทาง) warning sign. According to rule_id=182, this sign means that survey work is being conducted ahead on or near the road surface or carriageway, and drivers must slow down and exercise increased caution. Therefore, the correct action is to drive slowly and be careful, as survey personnel may be working on or near the road surface or bus lane.

questions.q_txt: From the picture, if you want to turn right You should be careful and how to act?

options.txt: Should turn to keep up because there is a large car blocking the car on the opposite side.
Speed up to turn right immediately.
Stop in the position to turn and let the opposite side to pass first.
Drive in the lane right side to make a turn.

questions.explanation: When turning right at a green light, Thai traffic law requires you to stop at the turning position and yield to oncoming traffic before completing the turn. Rule 161 (Section 22) states that even on a green signal, a driver turning must drive with caution and give right of way to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles coming from the opposite direction. Rule 215 further confirms that when turning right, the rider should stop at a distance from the center of the intersection to allow other vehicles to pass safely, and wait for a sufficient gap before turning — making option 3 the correct action.

questions.q_txt: What kind of parking may cause an accident?

options.txt: Parking in the parking building.
Park the car in the parking lot.
Park the car on the left edge of the road.
Double parking

questions.explanation: Double parking means parking a vehicle alongside another vehicle already parked at the road edge, effectively blocking that vehicle and protruding into the traffic lane. According to Section 54 (rule_id=151), drivers must park on the left side of the road with the vehicle parallel to and no more than 25 cm from the road edge — double parking violates this requirement and obstructs traffic flow, creating a serious accident hazard. The other options (parking buildings, designated parking lots, or the left road edge) are all lawful and safe parking methods as outlined in the safe parking guidelines (rule_id=217).

questions.q_txt: To remove the battery terminal which terminal should be disconnected first?

options.txt: Any pole first
Positive pole
Both terminals at the same time
Negative pole

questions.explanation: When removing a battery, the negative terminal must be disconnected first. This breaks the ground connection, so if the tool accidentally touches any metal part of the vehicle while removing the positive terminal afterward, no circuit is completed and no dangerous spark or short circuit can occur. Removing the positive terminal first would leave the circuit active, risking a short if the tool contacts the vehicle's grounded chassis.

questions.q_txt: If you park the car on the left side of the road And want to move out, what should you do?

options.txt: Look at the cars that follow through the side mirror and rear view mirror. Then turn on the right turn signal light.
Turn on the light to warn the following cars to slow down.
No need to look at the car parked in front. Looking at just the car that follows is enough.
Give a hand signal to ask for directions.

questions.explanation: When pulling out from a parked position on the left side of the road, you must first check your side mirrors and rearview mirror to assess the position and speed of following vehicles, then activate the right turn signal to alert other road users of your intention to move right into traffic (rule_id=242, rule_id=210). This procedure ensures you do not cause following vehicles to brake unexpectedly and that your intentions are clearly communicated at least 30 meters before the maneuver. Checking only following traffic via mirrors and signaling right is the correct and complete action required.

questions.q_txt: If adjustment of the driver’s seat is too far, what will be the effect?

options.txt: Make it easy to get into gear
Makes the visibility very clear, can make good decisions.
Difficulty controlling the steering wheel. Inconvenient use of equipment. Cannot use the clutch and brake in an emergency.
Make braking more convenient

questions.explanation: When the driver's seat is adjusted too far back (or too far forward), the rider cannot comfortably reach the handlebars, clutch lever, brake lever, and foot controls, making steering difficult and emergency braking or clutch operation impractical. As outlined in the riding posture guidelines (rule 199), proper body positioning—relaxed arms, hands centered on grips with fingers on the brake and clutch levers, and feet placed correctly on the footrests—is essential for effective vehicle control. If the seat distance is wrong, all of these posture requirements are compromised, directly leading to difficulty controlling the steering wheel and inability to operate the clutch and brake in an emergency.

questions.q_txt: What is the maximum size of the loaded object for automobile in length?

options.txt: Front side not exceeding bumper, back side not exceeding 2.50 meters from automobile body.
Front side not exceeding bumper, back side not exceeding 1 meters from automobile body.
Front side not exceeding 2.50 meters from automobile body, back side not exceeding bumper.
Front side not exceeding 1 meters from automobile body, back side not exceeding bumper.

questions.explanation: Under Thai road traffic regulations, when loading cargo onto an automobile, the load must not extend beyond the front bumper of the vehicle, and at the rear it must not extend more than 2.50 meters beyond the automobile body. This rule ensures that protruding loads remain within safe limits to avoid hazards to other road users. None of the provided rule chunks directly state this specific measurement, but option 1 (front not exceeding bumper, rear not exceeding 2.50 m) is the correct legal standard as established in the Road Traffic Act.

questions.q_txt: What is the correct conduct for the green car?

options.txt: Flash lights at the blue car allowing it to pass.
Drive ahead without stop
Stop the vehicle and wait for the blue car to pass.
Turn left directly

questions.explanation: The image shows a red STOP sign ('หยุด') at an intersection, which is a regulatory sign requiring the green car to come to a complete stop behind the stop line. Under rule_id=161 and rule_id=216, a red traffic sign bearing the word 'Stop' requires the driver to stop behind the stop line. Because the blue car is already in or passing through the intersection, rule_id=154 (Section 71) further requires the green car to yield and allow that vehicle to pass before proceeding.

questions.q_txt: When the blue car wants to turn what should be done?

options.txt: Sound car horn and flash lights to warn pedestrian while crossing.
Must stop and wait for the pedestrian to cross before turning.
Drive ahead directly.
Blue car should give way. Drive slowly through.

questions.explanation: The scene shows a blue car approaching a pedestrian crossing (zebra crossing) where a pedestrian is already crossing. According to the 'Caution Pedestrian Crossing' guidance (rule_id=180), if someone is crossing the road, drivers must stop to allow the pedestrian to cross safely before proceeding. Additionally, when making a turn at an intersection, drivers must give right of way to pedestrians in the crosswalk (rule_id=161), so the blue car must stop and wait until the pedestrian has fully crossed before turning.

questions.q_txt: From the picture, is this parking correct by the conduct?

options.txt: Yes, this is correct.
No, the driver must stop the car within at least 15 meters of the junction.
No, the driver must stop the car within at least 3 meters before the zebra crossing.
No, the driver cannot park on the left side of the road.

questions.explanation: The image shows a car parked directly beside or overlapping a zebra crossing (crosswalk), which is illegal under Thai traffic law. According to Section 55 of the Road Traffic Act, drivers are prohibited from stopping or parking within 3 meters before a crosswalk line, meaning the car must be kept at least 3 meters away from the crosswalk markings. The crosswalk line rule (rule_id=188) also reinforces that drivers must keep crosswalks clear so pedestrians can cross safely.

questions.q_txt: What is the correct conduct for the red car encountering obstacle ahead?

options.txt: Sound horn warning yellow car.
Wait for the yellow car to pass first before turning right and proceeding ahead.
Proceed ahead slowly with caution.
U-turn to avoid obstacle ahead.

questions.explanation: The image shows a red car that has encountered a road-narrowing obstacle (chevron/lane-merge sign) blocking its path, with a yellow car approaching in the adjacent lane. Because the red car must move right to pass the obstacle, it must first yield and wait for the oncoming yellow car to clear before turning right and proceeding — this aligns with the 'Alternate Merging' rule (rule_id=181), which instructs drivers to slow down and merge one vehicle at a time when a lane reduction is ahead, and with the general right-of-way principle (rule_id=239) requiring drivers to ensure it is safe before merging into another lane. Sounding the horn, proceeding without waiting, or making a U-turn would all risk a collision with the yellow car.

# Chapter 1: Laws Related to Driving

There are 4 important laws that drivers need to know, namely: the Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522, the Land Transport Act B.E. 2522, the Highway Act B.E. 2535, and the Road Traffic Act B.E. 2522.

## 1.1 Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522

Vehicles under the control of the Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522 consist of:

- Private passenger cars not exceeding 7 persons (sedans)
- Private passenger cars exceeding 7 persons but not exceeding 12 persons, which are not used for commercial transport for hire under the Land Transport Act
- Private trucks with a weight not exceeding 1,600 kilograms, which are not used for commercial transport for hire under the Land Transport Act
- Inter-provincial hire cars used for carrying passengers not exceeding 7 persons
- Hire cars for carrying passengers not exceeding 7 persons
- Service cars used for carrying passengers for hire or for rent not exceeding 7 persons
- Private motorcycles
- Public motorcycles
- Private three-wheeled vehicles
- Three-wheeled hire vehicles
- Road rollers
- Tractors
- Trailers
- Agricultural vehicles

### 1) Registration, Markings, and Use of Vehicles

1.1 Vehicles brought into use must be registered and have annual taxes fully and correctly paid. Any person who uses a vehicle without registration or tax payment shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 10,000 baht.

1.2 A vehicle eligible for registration must have complete and correct essential components and equipment as prescribed in the ministerial regulations and must have passed a vehicle inspection in accordance with the criteria, methods, and conditions prescribed in the ministerial regulations at the time of registration. Any person who uses a vehicle with incomplete or incorrect essential components or equipment as prescribed in the ministerial regulations, or adds anything that may cause harm to the body or mind of others, shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 baht.

1.3 To apply for vehicle registration, an application shall be submitted to the registrar of the locality where the applicant is domiciled.

1.4 A registered vehicle must have and display license plates and markings completely and correctly as prescribed in the ministerial regulations. Any person who violates this shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 baht.

1.5 Any change of vehicle color that differs from the registered color must be reported by the vehicle owner to the registrar within 7 days from the date of the color change. Any person who violates this shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 baht.

135.body:
1.6 For the transfer of a registered vehicle, both the transferor and the transferee must notify the registrar within 15 days from the date of transfer. Any person who violates this shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 baht.

1.7 When relocating a vehicle to a different locality, the vehicle owner must notify the local registrar within 15 days from the date of relocation. Any person who violates this shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 baht.

1.8 A registered vehicle shall not be altered in its body or any part thereof to differ from the registered particulars and then used, unless the owner first brings it to the registrar for inspection. Any person who violates this shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 baht.

1.9 "Red plates" are special markings issued by the Department of Land Transport to vehicle dealerships for use on vehicles only for the purpose of delivering them to customers or taking them for repairs. They are permitted to be driven only between sunrise and sunset, or during daytime only. The general public may not use red-plate vehicles on public roads at any time. If a vehicle bearing red plates that has not yet been registered and has not had its annual tax properly paid is used on the road, it constitutes an offense under the Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522, punishable by a fine not exceeding 10,000 baht.

2) Vehicles Exempt from Registration

2.1 Vehicles of the Royal Thai Police Department that are registered and bear markings as prescribed by the Director-General of the Royal Thai Police Department.

2.2 Vehicles of the Bureau of the Royal Household that are registered and bear markings as prescribed by the Secretary-General of the Royal Household.

2.3 Vehicles for which the owner has declared non-use.

2.4 Vehicles that the manufacturer or assembler has produced for sale, or that the importer has imported for sale, and that have been manufactured, assembled, or imported but have not yet been sold to others.

3) Vehicles Exempt from Fees, Except for License Plate Fees

3.1 Fire engines.

3.2 Ambulances that are not for-hire vehicles.

3.3 Vehicles of ministries, sub-ministries, departments, municipalities, provincial administrative organizations, sanitary districts, Bangkok Metropolitan Administration, Pattaya City, and other local government bodies — limited to vehicles not used for commercial purposes or profit.

3.4 Road rollers of state enterprises.

3.5 Tractors of state enterprises.

3.6 Vehicles of the Thai Red Cross Society.

3.7 Vehicles of persons in diplomatic missions, consular missions, international organizations, or specialized agencies of the United Nations stationed in Thailand.

3.8 Agricultural vehicles as specified by the characteristics and conditions prescribed in ministerial regulations.

4) Classification of Motor Vehicle Types and Seat Belt Designs

4.1 Notification of the Department of Land Transport regarding the specification of characteristics and installation of seat belts for motor vehicles, B.E. 2553, which shall not apply to small four-wheeled vehicles, small four-wheeled for-hire vehicles, three-wheeled private vehicles, and three-wheeled for-hire vehicles. The notification specifies two types of seat belts:

(1) Three-point belt (lap and shoulder belt)

(2) Lap belt

(3) Other motor vehicles not specified in (1) or (2), or motorcycles, shall be driven within the Bangkok Metropolitan Area, Pattaya City Area, or municipal areas at a speed not exceeding 80 kilometers per hour, or outside such areas at a speed not exceeding 70 kilometers per hour.

On roadways with traffic signs indicating a danger zone or a slow-driving zone, speed shall be reduced and caution increased as appropriate. In cases where traffic signs prescribe a speed limit lower than those specified above, the speed shall not exceed the speed limit so prescribed.

The Highway Act B.E. 2535 empowers the Minister to issue ministerial regulations prescribing speed limits for vehicles traveling on each category of highway, namely: the Ministerial Regulation Prescribing Speed Limits for Vehicles on Designated National Highways or Rural Highways B.E. 2564, which prescribes speed limits for vehicles on national highways or rural highways that have carriageways with at least two lanes in the same direction, a wall-type central median, and no at-grade U-turn points, as follows:

(1) Trucks with a vehicle weight exceeding 2,200 kilograms, or passenger vehicles with seating for more than fifteen passengers, shall travel at a speed not exceeding 90 kilometers per hour.

(2) Vehicles while towing other vehicles, small four-wheeled vehicles, or three-wheeled motor vehicles, shall travel at a speed not exceeding 65 kilometers per hour.

(3) Motorcycles shall travel at a speed not exceeding 80 kilometers per hour, except motorcycles with engine power of 35 kilowatts or more or with a combined cylinder displacement of 400 cubic centimeters or more, which may travel at a speed not exceeding 110 kilometers per hour.

(4) School buses or student transport vehicles shall travel at a speed not exceeding 80 kilometers per hour.

(5) Passenger vehicles with seating for more than seven but not more than fifteen passengers shall travel at a speed not exceeding 100 kilometers per hour.

(6) Tractors, road rollers, or agricultural vehicles shall travel at a speed not exceeding 45 kilometers per hour.

(7) Vehicles other than those in (1), (2), (3), (4), (5), and (6) shall travel at a speed not exceeding 120 kilometers per hour. In this regard, if such vehicle is in the rightmost lane, it must travel at a speed not less than 100 kilometers per hour, except where that lane has traffic restrictions, limited visibility, obstructions, or other impediments.

Clause 4: On roadways with traffic signs indicating a danger zone or a slow-driving zone, speed shall be reduced and caution increased as appropriate.

Clause 5: In cases where any roadway or traffic lane has traffic signs prescribing a speed limit lower than the rate prescribed in Clause 3, the speed shall not exceed the speed limit so prescribed.

3) Load Weight

The Highway Act B.E. 2535 empowers the Director of Highways for each category to issue announcements prohibiting the use of vehicles on highways where such vehicles have a weight, load weight, or axle weight exceeding the prescribed limits, or where such vehicles may cause damage to the highway. Violators shall be liable to imprisonment not exceeding 6 months or a fine not exceeding 10,000 baht, or both.

140.section: "Intersection" means the area where two or more roadways cross, converge, join, or adjoin each other.
140.body:
"Shoulder" means the area extending from the edge of the roadway outward to the side, which has not yet been constructed as a sidewalk.

"Intersection" means the area where two or more roadways cross, converge, join, or adjoin each other.

"Roundabout" means a roadway designated for vehicles to travel around a traffic sign or a structure built at an intersection.

"Sidewalk" means the area designated for pedestrians, located on one or both sides of the road, or the portion adjacent to the road edge used for pedestrian walking.

"Crosswalk" means the area designated for pedestrians to cross the road, marked with lines, markings, or studs on the road, and shall also include areas provided for pedestrians to cross whether at, below, or above ground level.

"Safety zone" means an area in the roadway that is clearly marked and visible at all times, designated for pedestrians crossing the road to stop and wait, or for persons boarding or alighting from vehicles to stop and wait before continuing to cross.

"Congested area" means a road with heavy traffic or obstructions, or a place where it can be foreseen that danger or damage to vehicles or persons may easily occur.

"Vehicle" means all types of land vehicles, except trains and trams.

"Motor vehicle" means a vehicle with three or more wheels that is propelled by engine power, electric power, or other energy, excluding vehicles that run on rails.

"Motorcycle" means a vehicle propelled by engine power, electric power, or other energy, having no more than two wheels; if a sidecar is attached, it may have no more than one additional wheel.

"Bicycle" means a vehicle propelled by the power of the rider, not being a vehicle that is dragged or pushed.

"Emergency vehicle" means fire engines and ambulances of the central government administration, regional government administration, and local government administration, or other vehicles authorized by the Director General to use flashing light signals or siren signals or other signals as may be prescribed.

"Truck" means a motor vehicle constructed for transporting goods or animals.

"Passenger vehicle" means a motor vehicle constructed for carrying more than 7 passengers.

"School bus" means a passenger vehicle used by a school to pick up and drop off students.

"Public bus" means a passenger vehicle that operates along a designated route and collects fares per person at rates set by distance or for the entire route.

"Taxi" means a motor vehicle used for hire to carry no more than 7 passengers.

"Tow truck" means a motor vehicle constructed for towing vehicles, agricultural equipment, or construction equipment, where the vehicle itself is not used for carrying persons or goods.

"Trailer" means a vehicle that is moved by being towed by another vehicle.

"Taximeter" means a device that displays the rate and fare of a taxi based on distance, time of taxi use, or both distance and time of taxi use.

"Driver" means a person who drives a vehicle, a person operating transport equipment under the law on transport, or a person dragging or pushing a vehicle.

"Pedestrian" means a person walking, and shall also include a person using a wheelchair for the disabled or a baby carriage.

"Vehicle owner" shall also include a person who has possession of the vehicle.

"Fare collector" means a person responsible for collecting fares and a person supervising passengers who is stationed on a passenger vehicle.
